# Quantum Illumination Feedback

An unknown static return phase can be learned with a paid set of pairwise measurements and one classical feedback update. The repository proves the resulting full-record error exponent, its strict classical comparison, and the failure of sublinear fixed-brightness pilots for a frozen one-output OPA receiver.

## Reading routes

- Question and main consequences: README.md, then science/interpretation.md.
- Physical introduction and notation from the single Shapiro2020 educational anchor: learning/README.md and learning/bridge.md. The anchor is The Quantum Illumination Story, using author manuscript arXiv:1910.12277v4 (23 December 2019).
- Project understanding targets and dependencies: learning/milestones.md, exactly M01–M30. M01–M12 assemble the background; M13–M30 connect the feedback mechanism to the complete contribution.
- State, channel, optical measurement, resource accounting and error convention: science/model.md.
- Exact adaptive-transcript law, large-sample theorem and weak-reflectivity allocation: science/error_exponent.md.
- Global strict advantage at specified nonzero reflectivity: science/finite_reflectivity.md.
- Classical benchmark and arbitrary mean-energy randomization: science/classical_limit.md.
- Why rare wrong settings matter: science/pilot_cost.md.
- Attribution and nearest adaptive proposals: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib.
- Reproducible calculations and their scope: verification/README.md.
- Exact-source GitHub mathematics and screenshot capture: verification/hosted_math/README.md.

## Preserve these distinctions

- The phase is common and constant, not redrawn between uses.
- All pilot signal uses and all pilot outcomes are counted.
- The leading expansion takes the large-sample limit before weak reflectivity.
- The exact fixed-reflectivity certificate still concerns a large-sample exponent.
- The optimum pilot fraction is only for the declared two-stage optical policy.
- The classical class is explicitly a mixture of conditionally coherent signals; a classical signal marginal alone does not meet that condition.
- The receiver needs ordinary idler storage and a local pump reference, but no quantum coherence between different pairs.
- The sublinear-pilot obstruction is for one frozen, one-output OPA setting. It does not cover every adaptive receiver.
- Finite numerical searches corroborate analytical results; they are not global proof certificates.
